title: SmoQyElPhQMC.jl: An open-source Julia package for efficient and scalable quantum Monte Carlo simulations of electron-phonon coupled models
authors: Benjamin Cohen-Stead, James Neuhaus, Kipton Barros, Thomas A. Maier, Steven Johnston
abstract: We introduce version 1.0 of the SmoQyElPhQMC package, an open-source Julia code for performing scalable quantum Monte Carlo simulations of electron-phonon coupled model Hamiltonians. SmoQyElPhQMC is built upon the SmoQyDQMC codebase and implements improved versions of the algorithms presented in [B. Cohen-Stead \textit{et al}., Phys. Rev. E {\bf 105}, 065302 (2022)] to enable linear-scaling simulations of a broad class of uncorrelated $e$-ph models both in system size and inverse temperature. By extending the functionality of the flexible scripting interface introduced in SmoQyDQMC, the SmoQyElPhQMC package continues to allow users to adapt it to different workflows and interface with other software packages in the Julia ecosystem. The code for this package can be downloaded from our GitHub repository at https://github.com/SmoQySuite/SmoQyElPhQMC.jl or installed using the Julia package manager. The online documentation, including examples, can be obtained from our documentation page at https://smoqysuite.github.io/SmoQyElPhQMC.jl/stable/.
summary: This work introduces an open-source Julia package, SmoQyElPhQMC.jl, designed for scalable Quantum Monte Carlo simulations of electron-phonon coupled models. By implementing advanced techniques like the Checkerboard Approximation and Kernel Polynomial Method preconditioning, it achieves near-linear scaling in system size and inverse temperature. The package is used to study phenomena such as charge density wave formation in canonical models like Holstein and oSSH.
main_problem: The primary goal is to perform efficient and scalable Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations for electron-phonon coupled models.
main_result: The package successfully enables near-linear scaling in system size and inverse temperature, allowing the study of CDW and BOW order formation in Holstein and oSSH models.
method: It utilizes advanced QMC techniques, including Hybrid Quantum Monte Carlo (HQMC) updates combined with the Checkerboard Approximation (MSCHK) and Kernel Polynomial Method (KPM) preconditioning for linear scaling.
model_or_system: The focus is on electron-phonon coupled Hamiltonians, specifically generalized spin-symmetric models like the Holstein model and the oSSH model. These systems involve coupling between itinerant electrons and lattice vibrations (phonons).
key_observables: Charge structure factor ($S_{cdw}$), bond order wave structure factor ($S_{bow}$), single-particle electron spectral function $A(k, \omega)$, and correlation functions.
important_parameters: The simulations are performed at finite temperatures ($ eta$) and involve coupling strengths ($\lambda_h=0.25$, $\lambda_o=0.36$) and phonon frequencies ($\Omega/t = 0.5$).
main_assumptions: Key approximations include the MSCHK approximation to reduce scaling from $O( eta N^3)$ to $O( eta N)$, and using pseudofermion fields for determinant calculation.
figures_summary: Figures show structure factors ($S_{cdw}, S_{bow}$) increasing with system size/inverse temperature, indicating CDW/BOW order. The spectral function $A(k, \omega)$ reveals gap openings consistent with insulating CDW order in the Holstein model.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the package, details the Hamiltonian structure ($\hat{H} = \hat{U} + \hat{V} + \hat{K}$), explains the mathematical machinery for achieving linear scaling (MSCHK, pseudofermion fields, KPM preconditioning), and concludes with benchmark results on Holstein and oSSH models.
why_interesting: The development of highly efficient numerical tools like SmoQyElPhQMC.jl to tackle strongly coupled lattice dynamics is crucial for understanding emergent quantum phases relevant to superconductivity and charge ordering in condensed matter systems.
